approachQuestion.prompt:
One Change in a Batch Code

Two batch codes have the same length. Return the zero-based index if exactly one position differs. Return −1 if the codes are identical or differ at two or more positions.

Example 1: referenceCode = "AX7Q", candidateCode = "AX9Q" → 2.
Example 2: referenceCode = "AB12", candidateCode = "CD12" → −1.
Example 3: referenceCode = "AB", candidateCode = "AB" → −1.
constraints: Both codes contain only ASCII characters (U+0000 through U+007F).
Do not modify either input string.

options.text: Compare characters at matching indices. Remember the first mismatch. Return −1 as soon as you find a second mismatch; otherwise return the remembered index, or −1 if there was no mismatch.
options.feedback: This accounts for both parts of the condition: a mismatch must exist, and there must be exactly one. After a second mismatch, the result cannot change.

options.text: Store every mismatch index in a list. Return the index only if the list contains exactly one item; otherwise return −1.
options.feedback: This method is correct for every allowed input. However, the list can hold many indices even though you only need the first index and whether a second mismatch exists.

options.text: Compare characters and return the first mismatch index immediately. Return −1 if no mismatch is found.
options.feedback: This does not check for a second mismatch. For "AB12" and "CD12", it returns 0 even though two positions differ; the correct result is −1.

options.text: Sort copies of both codes. If the sorted copies differ, return the first index where they differ; otherwise return −1.
options.feedback: Sorting makes positions refer to the sorted copies instead of the original codes. For "BAZ" and "BCZ", the only original mismatch is at index 1, but the first sorted mismatch is at index 0.

feedback.reason: Choose a method that distinguishes no mismatch, exactly one mismatch, and more than one mismatch.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the method “One Position Is Enough,” choose one pair: time and auxiliary space. The index and the marker for the first mismatch are auxiliary space; the input strings and returned value are excluded.
constraints: Both codes contain only ASCII characters (U+0000 through U+007F).
Do not modify either input string.

feedback.reason: Each compared index takes a fixed amount of work. The scan stops at the end or after the second mismatch. Regardless of the string length, it stores only a marker and one index.
details: linear-constant: the tight pair for a scan that stores one index.
linear-list: this describes collecting every mismatch index, as in option B.
quadratic-constant: repeatedly comparing pairs of characters is not part of the analyzed method.
constant: in the worst case, the entire code must be read to confirm there is no second mismatch.
Learning objective: Determine whether there is exactly one differing position; finding the first difference is not enough.

methodReveal.title: One Position Is Enough
methodReveal.description: Scan the matching indices. Store the first mismatch index, or mark that no mismatch has appeared yet. When you find a second mismatch, you can stop because the result is settled.
